facilities.name: Fairfax County I-66 Transfer Station (HHW & e-waste)
facilities.hours: Residents: trash, recycling and food scraps Mon–Fri 7am–5pm, Sat–Sun 7am–4pm. HHW and e-waste: Mon 7am–5pm; Tue and Thu 12–5pm; Fri 7am–5pm; Sat–Sun 7am–4pm; closed Wed. Holiday closures: see the county's holiday hours (complex closed Thanksgiving Day)
facilities.accepts: Household hazardous waste: aerosols, antifreeze and automotive fluids, gasoline, motor oil, rechargeable batteries, cooking oil, pool chemicals, household cleaners, lawn and garden chemicals and pesticides, oil-based paint, paint thinners, stains and varnish, mercury devices, CFLs and fluorescent tubes, propane tanks up to 20 lb; e-waste (TVs, computers, gaming systems, keyboards, speakers, cords); separated recycling incl. used motor oil, antifreeze and automobile batteries; bicycles; textiles; household trash. Not accepted at HHW: ammunition, explosives, illegal fireworks, LED bulbs, radioactive materials, hazardous waste pharmaceuticals, propane tanks over 20 lb, compressed gas cylinders, business hazardous waste
facilities.fees: Household hazardous waste is free for Fairfax County residents; common 20 lb barbecue propane tanks are accepted for a fee
facilities.notes: Operated by Fairfax County Department of Public Works and Environmental Services (Fairfax County, Virginia; it serves Fairfax County residents, not DC residents). Free HHW disposal is for Fairfax County residents only; proof of residency may be required (driver's license, state ID, property tax bill or utility bill). Business hazardous waste is not accepted. Latex paint: let it dry and put it in the trash, or bring cans you can't dry to the HHW area. HHW program: https://www.fairfaxcounty.gov/publicworks/recycling-trash/household-hazardous-waste; HHW questions 703-324-5230. I-66 Transfer Station 703-631-1179

facilities.accepts: Electronics (computers, monitors, keyboards, routers, phones, TVs, printers, fax machines, radios, stereo components, VCR/DVD players); paint (latex and oil-based), stain and varnish; rechargeable batteries (individually bagged) and lead-acid batteries (auto, marine, motorcycle); tires; appliances and bulky items; scrap metal; recycling drop-off. facilities.fees: Residential customers' annual solid waste assessment includes 10 cubic yards of bulky waste/appliance disposal per year and up to 12 tires per year; tires over 12 per year must go to the Southeast County Landfill at the tipping fee

Tires, bulky waste and appliances are only for County Solid Waste customers and also need a printed or digital copy of your current property tax bill; residents of Tampa, Temple Terrace and Plant City who pay a city for waste service should use their city's options for tires and bulky items. Limits: 5 intact electronic items per household per month (monitors, keyboards, routers and mice not counted); 10 one-gallon and 5 five-gallon paint containers per household per month; 12 tires per year. Businesses are not authorized to use CCCs. Hand unloading only. Paint/electronics limits: https://hcfl.gov/residents/property-owners-and-renters/trash-and-recycling/discarding-paint-and-electronics. facilities.name: Kiefer Landfill (tires, e-waste & ABOP drop-off)
facilities.hours: Landfill: Mon–Fri 6:30am–4:30pm; Sat–Sun 8:30am–4:30pm (arrive at least 15 minutes before closing; may close early if the daily vehicle limit is reached). Thanksgiving Day closes at 2pm; Christmas and New Year's Day close at 2pm on weekdays, all day on weekends. facilities.accepts: Free residential drop-off: passenger/light-truck tires (rims OK, 4 per day free), e-waste (TVs, CRTs, monitors, computers, laptops, tablets, phones, printers, gaming consoles, stereos), large appliances (2 per day free), small corded appliances and power tools, mattresses and box springs, clean metal, clean inerts. ABOP & Special Waste facility (residents): antifreeze, household and car batteries, motor oil and filters, cooking oil, latex and oil-based paint, aerosol cans, brake/transmission fluid, fluorescent tubes and bulbs (12 tubes per month), home-generated sharps in sealed containers, mercury thermometers and switches, barbecue propane tanks (limit two). Not accepted at ABOP: acids, household cleaners, pesticides and herbicides, solvents, paint thinners, gasoline, pool chemicals, ammunition, explosives, medical waste. Products with built-in batteries go to the e-waste area. Also takes household trash, green waste and treated wood (fees)
facilities.fees: Free for residents: tires 1–4 per day, e-waste, appliances 1–2 per day, mattresses, clean metal, and ABOP items up to 15 gallons or 125 pounds per month (a load must contain only free items). facilities.name: Goochland Central Convenience Center
facilities.hours: Daily 7:30am–6pm (closed county holidays and other announced closures)
facilities.accepts: Automobile tires (fee; up to 19 in. on or off rim, 19–24 in. off rim, agricultural tires 24.5–42 in. off rim); used motor oil, automatic transmission and power-steering fluid, gear and hydraulic oil, diesel and fuel oil (oil drum); oil filters; antifreeze; leaded/unleaded gasoline, motor-oil additives, oil-based paint, stains, varnish/shellac, polyurethane, primer, lacquer and paint thinners, mineral spirits and turpentine (paint drums); rechargeable and lead-acid batteries; propane tanks; electronics at the permanent electronics trailer (computers, laptops, monitors, printers, keyboards, TVs, stereos, VCRs, cell phones; small consumer appliances, power tools, fans and lamps not accepted in the electronics program); appliances/white goods (Freon recovery); household trash; drop-off recycling (mixed paper, cans, plastic containers #1–7, cartons, glass)
facilities.fees: Free for county residents for household trash and recyclables. Tires: up to 19 in. off rim $2, up to 19 in. on rim $6, 19–24 in. off rim $13, agricultural tires 24.5–42 in. off rim $30 (large loads may be referred to a landfill). Fees also apply to air conditioners, brush and refrigerators/Freon appliances
facilities.notes: Operated by Goochland County; county residents only with proof of residency (County Code Sec. 7-71: only county residents may use county-owned waste facilities). Motor oil, paint/solvent and electronics locations per the Central Virginia Waste Management Authority Goochland recycling guide: https://cvwma.com/recycling/goochland/. County Code Sec. 7-71 also lists hazardous waste, solvents and oil among items not to be disposed of at county facilities, so use only the designated oil and paint drums and ask the attendant before unloading. Latex paint: county says dry it out completely and put it in the trash. 804-556-5374

facilities.name: E-Opala (e-waste drop-off, Māpunapuna)
facilities.accepts: Covered electronic devices under Hawaii's Electronic Device Recycling and Recovery Law: computers, monitors, laptops, tablets and e-readers, printers, TVs (9 in. screen or larger), fax machines, VCRs, DVD players and recorders, portable digital music players, household routers and modems, and peripherals (keyboards, mice, cords, power supplies and adapters, computer or TV speakers and sound bars, video game consoles)
facilities.notes: Listed by the Hawaii State Department of Health as an Oahu (City & County of Honolulu) collection location for covered electronic devices. Pick-up collection is available for a fee (contact E-Opala for a quote). (808) 232-2000. Oahu residents can also use the City's e-waste bins at its convenience centers and transfer stations
